title: Towards Understanding Professional AI Assistant Use: Human-in-the-Loop Topic Modeling of Multi-turn Conversations
venue: Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW Companion)
subcategory: LLM summarisation + density clustering + human in the loop
task: Topic discovery over multi-turn user-assistant conversations
problem: Word-based topic models do not capture the task behind multi-turn assistant conversations; topics must stay current as new data arrives.
architecture: HILTON: conversation-turn extraction; few-shot LLM task summaries; all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings, standardisation, UMAP to 50-d, HDBSCAN (min cluster size 150, min samples 5) with iterative noise re-clustering and constrained Voronoi reassignment of outliers; LLM cluster naming with contrastive samples, hierarchisation and deduplication; annotator review; KNN classifier for new data with probability threshold; max-min and stratified sampling to keep the embedding database compact.

datasets.name: Data provided by the company (AI-assistant conversations)
datasets.details: about 50k task summaries; data and statistics not disclosed

key_results: GPT-4o-mini summaries agree most with other LLMs (e.g. BLEU-1 56.22 against GPT-nano).
Inter-annotator agreement: alpha 0.7348 for summary consistency, 0.4941 for sub-cluster names, 0.5298 for higher-level names.
Outlier reassignment stabilises after about five rounds (Silhouette 0.3344 at round 5).
strengths: End-to-end deployable pipeline: discovery, human curation, incremental updates and cheap classification of new conversations.
Operates on embeddings and summaries, which the authors argue is privacy-preserving.

limitations.text: Data cannot be disclosed, which limits reproducibility.
No comparison with other topic models; quality is reported through internal cluster indices and annotator agreement only.
